chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Samaan, who said:

I asked him about those witnesses whose testimony is rejected, so he said: 'The doubtful one, the litigant, the partner, the bearer of a burden/debt, the hired worker, the slave, the follower, and the suspected one — all of these, their testimonies are rejected.'

key_terms.الْخَصْمُ: the litigant (one involved in a lawsuit)
key_terms.الْمُرِيبُ: the doubtful one (one who is uncertain about the matter)

ai.seo_question: Who are the witnesses whose testimony is rejected in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific categories of individuals whose testimony is rejected, emphasizing the jurisprudential criteria of *‘udul* (uprightness) and absence of conflict of interest. It highlights key disqualifiers such as the *murib* (one with doubt in faith), *khasm* (adversary), and *muttaham* (suspected of dishonesty), reflecting the Shia emphasis on both moral integrity and legal impartiality in judicial proceedings.
